body_long:
Weissenhaus has a new general manager. Mathias Gerds takes charge of Weissenhaus Private Nature Luxury Resort, on the Baltic coast of Schleswig-Holstein, on 1 December 2026. The German trade press announced the appointment on 24 November. His start was brought forward to allow a smooth handover with Martin Elsner, who leaves as planned at the end of February 2027.

## A career across three continents

Born in Rostock, Gerds began as F&B manager at Grand Hotel Heiligendamm from 2007 to 2009, then held the same role at Palais Coburg in Vienna. His first general manager post was Hotel auf der Wartburg in Thuringia. He then worked for Kempinski in China and Russia, became hotel manager at Anantara Siam Bangkok and St. Regis Kuala Lumpur, and led the two Six Senses properties in Singapore.

In 2019 he took over Six Senses Residences Courchevel 1850, and in summer 2021 he oversaw the opening of Six Senses Ibiza. After Kisawa Sanctuary in Mozambique, he returned to Grand Hotel Heiligendamm as director in December 2023, before leaving in October 2025 for Raffles London at The OWO.

## A private world on the Baltic

Weissenhaus covers more than 75 hectares, with 3 km of beach, a castle over 400 years old and a spa of 3,000 m². It has been a Relais & Châteaux member since 2018 and holds two MICHELIN Keys. Its owner and founder, Jan Henric Buettner, describes Gerds as a hotelier who knows both top-hotel standards and personal hospitality. For Gerds, "exceptional hotels are not created by architecture or furnishings alone".

## The signal

German resorts are recruiting leaders shaped by the world's biggest luxury brands. Experience gained with Six Senses and Raffles is now coming home to a family-owned estate.

Congratulations to Mathias Gerds on his new role.
summary: The former Raffles London at The OWO and Six Senses hotelier becomes general manager of Weissenhaus on the Baltic coast on 1 December 2026.
title: Mathias Gerds, from Raffles London to Weissenhaus
why: A Six Senses and Raffles résumé takes over Germany's most private Baltic estate.
